title: Universal model improvements: Introducing advanced contextual text formatting for Spanish and German

body_text: We have released new and improved models since this article was published. See our docs for our most current model offerings. Upgrade your multilingual transcriptions with formatting that native speakers prefer—now achieving 62.2% preference rates for Spanish and 54.5% for German. Multilingual transcription challenges Getting the words right is only half the battle. Without proper punctuation, capitalization, and formatting, even accurate transcriptions can feel awkward and unprofessional to native speakers. That's why we've upgraded our Universal Speech-to-Text model with advanced text formatting capabilities specifically designed for Spanish and German—two languages with unique formatting requirements that standard transcription services often overlook. Why contextual text formatting matters Text formatting directly impacts how users experience and trust your transcriptions: Enhanced Comprehension : Proper punctuation placement guides readers through complex sentences effortlessly Professional Credibility : Language-specific formatting rules (like German noun capitalization) demonstrate cultural awareness Natural Flow : Contextual number formatting makes transcriptions feel authentically native Improved Accessibility : Grammar-aware formatting reduces cognitive load for all users Four breakthrough improvements that set Universal apart Our enhanced model is based on the Universal all-neural architecture that we introduced last year for English and trained on a large text corpus for target languages. This yields the following advantages for our model. 1. Precision punctuation that respects language nuances Our enhanced model is now a fully trained end to end neural network that doesn't just understand punctuation logic, but also the cultural and grammatical context it operates in: Spanish-specific punctuation : Automatic insertion of inverted question marks (¿) and exclamation points (¡) exactly where native speakers expect them Intelligent comma placement : Context-aware decisions that reflect natural speech patterns Period identification : Sophisticated algorithms that accurately locate periods and parse sentence boundaries Measurable impact : Our punctuation accuracy shows significant improvements with relative Punctuation Error Rate reduced by 15.3% for Spanish (from 30.8% to 26.1%) and 19.2% for German (from 22.9% to 18.5%). title: Towing Marketing: 6 Strategies and Best Practices for 2025
summary: Explore effective towing marketing strategies to grow your business. Learn how to get more towing business with proven advertising ideas and advanced marketing tactics.
body_text: Like any service-based company, towing businesses must deliver exceptional customer service or risk becoming irrelevant. Following best practices in marketing can help towing businesses unlock new sources of revenue and gain market share. The right path can set them on a course to stand out, attract new customers, and cultivate long-term customer relationships. These businesses have their work cut out for them, however. Successful towing companies have found ways to overcome challenges like a crowded marketplace. In any given market, there could be dozens of companies, and you need to give consumers a reason to select one over another. It also doesn’t help that customers will call you in a pinch (and in a panic) and don’t need your services on a regular basis. The one-off nature means it’s more challenging to gain long-term customers. On a related note, some customers hold a negative view of towing companies. You might have to prove you’re trustworthy— and that can take some effort to get started on the right foot. 6 Tow Truck Marketing Strategies Towing companies can make investments in proven marketing strategies to win customers . A few of the most common and effective include the following: Retargeting Ads Retargeting helps you command the attention of customers who have visited your website but didn’t follow up. Specifically, you can display targeted ads on websites and apps to re-engage potential customers. Top-of-mind awareness can work to your advantage here. Content Marketing Content marketing is all about educating your target customers about your industry. Your content marketing strategy should include blog posts related to car maintenance, how to handle roadside emergencies, and when to call for help. Cross-promote these pieces on your social media channels to amplify your message. PPC Advertising Also known as pay-per-click advertising, you can take advantage of platforms like Google Ads to reach prospects based on specified keywords and backgrounds. Make sure your website and landing pages reinforce your messaging and draw the reader in. Reputation Management Check review sites regularly and address glowing and less flattering ones as soon as possible. Make it a part of your processes and procedures to ask for reviews on Google, Yelp and the like. You can invest in reputation management tools to keep you plugged into customer sentiment and respond faster. Email Marketing Email marketing is relatively inexpensive and fairly easy to implement. Start by entering the email addresses of past towing customers and prospects. From here, you can push out monthly updates with discounts, company news, and tips. Emails can help you court prospects and push them through the sales funnel. SMS Marketing Text messaging offers a similar use case as email marketing, and it’s also accessible in terms of cost. You can create text-based campaigns to send appointment reminders, status updates, and other relevant touchpoints. When in doubt, SMS marketing is great for simple and mass communication. These marketing tactics can lay the foundation for towing companies to attract new customers and become the company of choice in their market. How to Leverage Towing Advertising Knowing how and when to advertise is how towing companies can entice prospects to make the call. The right approach and execution are how they can get noticed, attract leads , and hit sales goals. First and foremost, all ads should communicate a sense of urgency. You should be the name that comes to mind when they’re panicking and need help. Stress your reliable reputation and professionalism and how you’ll come to their rescue when it matters the most. Vehicle wraps can present a positive brand image, while giving you 24/7 exposure through truck advertising. The art should reflect your company marketing and brand palette. The call to action should be clear and to the point. Important details like your phone number and website should be easy to read. Beyond traditional advertising channels, you might consider investments in community events. Think festivals, sports tournaments, and charity fundraisers. You also might find success aligning with other local businesses and promoting each other. This can make your advertising and marketing dollars go further. Video marketing is another way to reach people online. The sky’s the limit when it comes to the type of content you could make. For instance, tutorials on how to change a flat can help position you as the expert in towing services. Customer testimonials are great in a video format because they offer more dimension than a text-based review. You also might feature a “day on the job” type of content to give customers and prospects a window into how your tow truck business works. When it comes to success with social media more broadly, it’s important to share regularly on a mix of platforms, like Facebook, X, Instagram and TikTok. Be sure your content is helpful and even entertaining—not just promotional—or people will be turned off. Be sure to keep tabs on activity on all your social media accounts and respond to comments, questions and other engagement. Best Towing Advertising Ideas for 2024 Towing companies might find their efforts go further when they allocate funds to online advertising. Here’s a look at a few of the most popular channels and tips to get better results. Google Ads Build your ads around phrases like “tow truck near me” or “emergency towing.” Use geo-targeting so you don’t waste your budget on showing ads to people outside your service area. Be sure your call-to-action is specific. Facebook Ads Your ads should be visually engaging and get your point access. Use Facebook’s targeting abilities to reach people who fit your ideal customer profile. Monitor your ad performance and adjust course as needed. Instagram Ads Post photos and videos that show how you help people solve their problems. Instagram Stories are a great way to capture moments on the job that you can’t anticipate. Tap the expertise and networks of influencers to increase your reach. How to Get More Towing Business You can’t expect your phone lines to be flooded with new customers overnight. Rather, growing your customer base is all about strategy. These tips can help set your towing company up for success: 1. Elevate Your Online Presence How easily customers can find you online and what they read about you influences buying decisions. That said, you’ll want to make sure your Google Business Profile is fleshed out and current. Take inventory of all important details like address, phone number, and website. You don’t want to lose business because something is dated. Ask customers for reviews after each job. You could even offer a discount on their next service as an incentive. Your website is equally as important when it comes to search ranking and inquiries. Your site should be easy to navigate and communicate your offerings. Be sure you’re using relevant keywords so search engines will rank you higher. 2. Provide Exceptional Customer Service In moments of crisis, great customer service can save the day. Be sure your team is responding to requests for help promptly and courteously. Arrive at job sites as quickly as possible and respect the customer’s time. Always be sure to inform them of your prices and how you collect payment upon scheduling so they know what to expect. 3. Use Digital Marketing Digital marketing can be your ticket to getting more jobs. Pay-per-click advertising like Google Ads helps you target people who might be in need of towing services. Similarly, targeted ads on Facebook and Instagram can help you get in front of potential customers. Content marketing offers the same value proposition. You can create educational blog posts and video tutorials to capture interest and drive traffic to your website. Last, email marketing helps you engage with your customers in a way that allows you to track results. 4. Build Strong Community Relationships Your customers live, work, and play in your service area. They likely want to do business with a familiar name and someone who cares about the well-being of its residents. Being invested in your community can create a positive association with your brand. For instance, you can underwrite the cost of charity fundraisers and community-wide celebrations. You could consider joining forces with other businesses to help your dollars go further. 5. Optimize Your Google Business Profile It’s a good idea to audit your Google Business Profile every now and then. For instance, photos and videos can help generate interest. Make a point to respond to reviews. Double-check that all location information is accurate. For example, if you recently changed addresses, you’ll need to make sure the directory information aligns to avoid creating undue confusion. 6. Encourage Customer Reviews Encourage customers to create profiles on Google, Yelp, and other review sites to detail their experience with your towing company. Acknowledge both positive and negative ones and thank them for their feedback. Transform Your Towing Marketing with Podium Podium can help towing businesses grow the smart way. Business owners can use it to manage and boost online reputation, engage with customers through features like chat and text messaging, and bring in more business. Trying these strategies alongside a proven tool like Podium can help towing businesses rank higher online and achieve sales goals. title: NewcelX Announces Successful FDA Pre-IND Meeting with Clear Path Forward for NCEL-101 Toward Starting Clinical Trials for Type 1 Diabetes
summary: FDA feedback supports NewcelX’s planned development strategy for NCEL-101 in combination with Tegoprubart...
body_text: ZURICH, July 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NewcelX Ltd. (“NewcelX”; Nasdaq: NCEL), a clinical-stage regenerative medicine company developing stem-cell-derived therapies, announced the successful completion of its Type B Pre-IND meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”). The agency provided constructive feedback and alignment on the Company’s proposed development strategy, providing clarity regarding the regulatory pathway toward launching a clinical trial of NCEL-101 for type 1 diabetes in combination with Eledon Pharmaceuticals’ (Nasdaq: ELDN) anti-CD40L antibody, tegoprubart, an investigational immunomodulatory agent. The meeting results represent a significant milestone toward the clinical development of an innovative treatment paradigm targeting a potential functional cure for type 1 diabetes. The FDA provided favorable feedback on NewcelX's Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (“CMC”) processes and preclinical program allowing the Company to proceed toward its Investigational New Drug (“IND”) enabling activities. Ronen Twito, CEO & Executive Chairman of NewcelX, added, “Coming out of our FDA meeting, we have a well-defined clinical path forward and strengthened confidence in our development approach. We are fully committed to bringing NCEL-101 into the clinic as quickly as possible with the goal of developing a potentially transformative treatment for patients with type 1 diabetes.” "We are excited to explore the combination of tegoprubart with NewcelX's advanced islet cell therapy," added Dr. David-Alexandre Gros, CEO of Eledon Pharmaceuticals . "By combining tegoprubart's demonstrated ability to protect transplanted tissue with NCEL-101's cell platform, we are collectively moving closer to a potential fully scalable therapeutic option for individuals living with type 1 diabetes." Combining NCEL-101, an enriched stem cell-derived islet product candidate, with Eledon’s anti-CD40L monoclonal antibody, tegoprubart, serving as the cornerstone of a calcineurin inhibitor-free immunosuppressive regimen is designed to enable durable graft survival and function, with the goals of achieving outcomes comparable to donor human islet transplantation. This body of clinical transplant experience provides important safety, dosing, and immunologic insights that are directly relevant to islet cell replacement therapies and support the planned advancement of NCEL-101. title: AWS Now Decides Whether You Get a Rep. Here's How That Decision Gets Made.
summary: AWS now scores every co-sell opportunity in real time and routes it to a motion. What the score measures, why half of zeros are template text, and how Suger fixes it pre-submission.
body_text: Introducing co-sell quality prediction, AI-generated business problems, and predicted AWS contacts in Suger. On June 16, 2026, AWS made it official: Partner Central agents now qualify every co-sell opportunity in real time. Every opportunity receives an Opportunity Quality Score that “measures co-sell readiness and directly influences how AWS engages.” Each opportunity is now matched to one of three co-sell motions: AWS field-engaged — an AWS sales team collaborates directly on your deal. Agent-engaged — the agent strengthens your submission to try to earn AWS engagement. Partner-led — you drive the deal yourself, with agent support. The score determines which one you get. And the motion recalculates in real time as the opportunity improves. So co-sell is no longer a queue you wait in. It’s a threshold you either clear at submission or don’t. A weak referral doesn’t get ignored anymore — it gets formally routed to “Partner-led,” which is a polite way of saying you’re on your own. That makes one question urgent for every ISV: what actually moves the score? Finding #1: the score has nothing to do with your deal Every single LOWEST referral scored exactly 0. Not 12, not 8. Zero. Every HIGHEST referral landed between 50 and 75. Note the ceiling: even AWS’s own “best” examples top out at 75. Nobody is anywhere near 100. There is enormous headroom in a field where most submissions are scoring nothing. Deal size didn’t correlate. Neither did expected AWS revenue, industry, or region. What the score measures is narrative completeness — whether an AWS seller (or now, an agent deciding your motion) can read your referral and immediately know who the customer is, what’s broken, why they have to act now, and what you need from AWS. It rewards a specific, actionable customer story. It punishes empty templates and product pitches. Which means the thing gating your access to AWS field engagement is, functionally, the quality of a paragraph. Finding #2: there are two completely different ways to fail This is the part that surprised us. The referrals scoring zero weren’t losing on nuance. Nearly half of them were submitted with the template still sitting in the field — placeholder bullets, unanswered prompt questions like “what is the customer trying to solve?”, boilerplate stubs nobody deleted. A third had no customer context at all. A third described what the ISV’s product does instead of what the customer needs. These aren’t storytelling failures. They’re submissions that were never really written. And they appear to be unrecoverable — no amount of detail elsewhere in the record pulls them out of a zero. The HIGHEST-scoring referrals, meanwhile, were missing many of the same finer details as the zeros: no concrete ask of AWS, no named customer contact, no quantified scope. Those gaps are near-universal. They are not what separates the buckets. What separates the buckets is whether anyone wrote a real customer story at all. That’s the whole game, and it splits into two very different problems: Tier one — the zeros. Empty templates, product pitches, blank required fields. High volume, entirely mechanical, and completely preventable. Tier two — the ceiling. Even good submissions leave points on the table on the refinements. Worth optimizing, but only after tier one is solved. Most ISVs think they have a tier-two problem. Our data says the majority have a tier-one problem they don’t know about, because nobody sees the referral again after it leaves the CRM. The encouraging part: every signal the score rewards is either already sitting in your CRM or is one question away from the rep who’s on the deal. Almost none of it requires new information. It requires the information to make it into the right field, in the right form, before you hit submit. Which is exactly what we built. What we shipped AWS’s agent will recommend improvements after you submit, and the score recalculates. That’s genuinely better than the old silence. But it’s still a loop that starts after your deal has been sorted into a motion — and after your rep has moved on to the next thing. We’d rather you never submit a zero. So we moved the evaluation upstream, into the submission itself. 1. Predicted quality score, before you submit Suger now shows a live Predicted AWS quality score on the co-sell submission screen, broken out by dimension, with the specific fixes ranked by how many points they’re worth. It reads like AWS reads. A submission that scores 52 tells you why: This opportunity contains a strong compelling event, clear requirements, and is well-quantified. However, it is critically undermined by an apparent copy-paste error, as the customer is ‘Spyce’ but the business problem describes ‘Northwind.’ It also completely lacks next steps and competitive details. +25 Rewrite the Customer business problem to be about the actual customer, removing incorrect references. Add a specific ask for AWS. +15 Add a Next step with a concrete action, a target date, and the customer contact involved. +8 In Competitive tracking, name the incumbent or competing vendors being evaluated. Apply those and the same record hits 92 — with a single 8-point gap left on competitive tracking. That’s not a marginal improvement. In the new motion model, that’s the difference between “Partner-led” and “AWS field-engaged” on a deal you already had. The gate checks run as hard validation. Everything else is a nudge with a point value attached, so your reps know exactly what a fix is worth and stop guessing. 2. AI-generated business problems in field mapping The bigger unlock is that you don’t have to write the narrative at all. Suger’s field mapping already pulls your Salesforce data into every co-sell field. We added an AI generation option on any field — including the Customer Business Problem, the field that carries more weight in the score than anything else in the record. Instead of piping your raw opportunity description straight through (which is how the template text and product pitches get in there), you configure a prompt once. It reads the account name, industry, close date, renewal date, AWS services in scope, competitors, use-case notes, and expected spend from the opportunity, and drafts the strongest customer-centric business problem those facts support. Configure it once, and every referral your team pushes clears the gates by construction. Three rules matter in that prompt: Write about the customer, never the product. A product pitch scores 0. The prompt has to be explicitly forbidden from describing your own capabilities. Use only facts present in the data. This text goes to AWS as a factual claim about a real customer. No invented deadlines, dollar figures, contacts, or compliance standards — ever. Never emit placeholders. If a fact is missing, write around it. Then surface the gap to the submitter as a data gap, rather than papering over it. The output is a tight narrative that names the customer, anchors urgency to a real date, names the AWS services and compliance requirements in play, and closes with one concrete ask — plus a list of the two or three missing fields that would raise the score most if the rep filled them in. You go from your reps writing 200 co-sell descriptions a quarter to your reps only reviewing the auto-generated drafts. 3. When the score still isn’t enough: predicted AWS contacts Even a well-scored referral can land in “Agent-engaged” or “Partner-led.” AWS coverage is finite, territories shift, and no number on a form guarantees a human on the other end. So Suger doesn’t make the score your only path to an AWS human. If the motion model doesn’t hand you a rep, we’ll tell you who the rep could have been. Our account mapping layer maintains a database of cloud reps across AWS, Azure, and GCP — enriched with the domains each rep actually manages, their industries, coverage location, region, account count, open pipeline, closed-won, and success rate. When you open an opportunity, Suger surfaces the predicted contacts for that account: the specific AWS sellers whose book of business already includes that customer domain. That means if your referral doesn’t get an assignment through the ACE queue, you’re not stuck waiting. You have a named rep, their track record, and the accounts they cover — surfaced right in the Salesforce widget on the opportunity, not buried in a spreadsheet someone maintained six months ago. Earnings Available for Distribution The Company's business objective is to provide attractive risk-adjusted returns to its stockholders, primarily through dividends and secondarily through capital appreciation. The Company may add and has added additional reconciling items to its earnings available for distribution calculation as appropriate. By excluding the gains and losses discussed above, the Company believes the presentation of earnings available for distribution provides a consistent measure of operating performance that investors can use to evaluate its results over multiple reporting periods and, to a certain extent, compare to its peer companies. The Company excludes the impact of gains and losses when calculating earnings available for distribution because when analyzed in conjunction with its U.S. GAAP results, earnings available for distribution provides additional detail of its investment portfolio's earnings capacity. In addition, certain gains and losses represent one-time events. Furthermore, gains and losses have not been accounted for consistently under U.S. GAAP. Under U.S. GAAP, certain gains and losses may be reflected in net income whereas other gains and losses may be reflected in other comprehensive income. For example, a portion of the Company's mortgage-backed securities were historically classified as available-for-sale securities, and changes in the valuation of these securities were recorded in other comprehensive income on its condensed consolidated balance sheets. The Company elected the fair value option for its mortgage-backed securities purchased on or after September 1, 2016, and changes in the valuation of these securities are recorded in other income (loss) in the condensed consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss). To maintain qualification as a REIT, U.S. federal income tax law generally requires that the Company distribute at least 90% of its REIT taxable income annually. Because the Company views earnings available for distribution as a consistent measure of its investment portfolio's ability to generate income for distribution to common stockholders, earnings available for distribution is one metric, but not the exclusive metric, that is used to determine the amount, if any, of dividends on common stock. Earnings available for distribution is an incomplete measure of the Company's financial performance and there are other factors that impact the achievement of the Company's business objective. title: How to Build a Productive Dorm Room Desk Setup
summary: Turn three feet of dorm desk into a real workstation. Monitor, keyboard, and space-saving picks with verified Newegg prices.
body_text: A dorm desk gives you roughly three feet of territory in which to study, write, game, video-call home, and occasionally eat instant noodles. It is simultaneously your office, your library, your theater, and the only square footage in the building that is truly yours. The difference between a desk that fights you all semester and one that quietly makes you better is not money, and it is definitely not size; it is a handful of deliberate choices made once, in the right order. Here is how to turn a cramped slab of university furniture into the most productive corner of your room, zone by zone, with real prices checked on Newegg at this writing. Who Needs This? Anyone whose entire workspace, bedroom, and living room share one address. The constraints of dorm life are stubbornly physical: a desk with little depth, walls you cannot drill into, a roommate whose sleep schedule inverts yours during midterms, and a laptop that was never designed for six-hour hunched-over writing sessions. There is also a constraint nobody warns freshmen about: visual chaos. In a room where your bed is visible from your desk and your desk is visible from your bed, a cluttered workspace quietly taxes your focus every waking hour. Every recommendation below attacks one of these constraints directly, and the whole plan is modular, so you can build it across two semesters of budgets instead of one painful checkout. Zone 1: The Screen, Where Posture Is Won or Lost A 27-inch QHD panel like the Pixio PX275 Wave doubles usable screen space over a laptop. Ask any ergonomist, or any senior with a physical therapy bill, and they will tell you the same thing: the single most transformative upgrade for a laptop-bound student is an external monitor raised to eye level. The reason is anatomical. A laptop screen forces your gaze, and therefore your neck, downward by twenty degrees or more, and your shoulders follow. Hours of that posture, repeated daily, is how twenty-year-olds develop what clinicians politely call tech neck. Raise the screen so its top edge sits at eye height and the problem largely disappears. The productivity math is just as compelling. A 27-inch panel at 2560×1440 resolution offers roughly 1.8 times the pixels of a typical 1080p laptop display, which in practice means a research paper and its sources genuinely side by side, a spreadsheet showing enough columns to be useful, or code and documentation sharing the screen without the alt-tab dance that fragments attention. The Pixio PX275 Wave , a 27-inch 1440p IPS monitor listed at $189.99 at this writing, is exactly this kind of do-everything panel: IPS color that keeps photos and films looking right from any seating angle, a 100Hz refresh rate that makes scrolling silky and casual gaming legitimately enjoyable after hours, and a white finish that keeps a small room feeling airy rather than looming over it. Whatever monitor you choose, resist the included stand. Factory stands plant a foot the size of a dinner plate in the exact center of your only work surface. A clamp-style arm bolts to the rear edge of the desk instead, floats the screen above everything, and returns a laptop-sized patch of prime real estate to you instantly; browse single monitor arms on Newegg , where most models install in ten minutes with nothing but the included hex key and support far more weight than any 27-inch panel requires. Zone 2: The Input Deck, Small but Mighty A 75% wireless board keeps the typing feel and gives back mouse space. Full-size keyboards waste a third of their width on a number pad most students touch twice a semester, and on a shallow dorm desk that stolen width comes directly out of your mouse hand’s territory. The fix is the 75% layout, which keeps every key students actually use, including the full function row for lecture-recording shortcuts and the arrow cluster essay editing depends on, in a footprint dramatically narrower than the boards most people grew up with. The Womier WD75 V2 ($93.99) is a snapshot of how absurdly good this category has become at student prices. Tri-mode connectivity means it pairs over Bluetooth with your laptop, links via a low-latency 2.4GHz dongle to a desktop, and falls back to USB-C wired when you forget to charge, though with an 8000mAh battery, forgetting takes weeks. The switches are hot-swappable, meaning that if your roommate objects to clacking during 1 a.m. essay sprints, you can pull the switches and drop in silent ones without touching a soldering iron. Gasket mounting and a wood-accented case make it feel like a hobbyist board, and QMK/VIA support lets you remap any key, so the pause key you never use can become a mute button for surprise video calls. One under-appreciated note: a good keyboard outlives everything else on this list. Laptops get replaced, monitors get upgraded, but a quality mechanical board follows you from dorm to apartment to first job. Cost per year of service, it is arguably the best value on the desk. Zone 3: The Connection Hub, One Cable to Rule Them All Picture the daily workflow you actually want: walk in from class, drop your bag, plug a single USB-C cable into the laptop, and everything comes alive, monitor, keyboard, mouse dongle, and charging, all at once. That is not a luxury flagship-office feature anymore; it is what any decent USB-C docking station does for well under a hundred dollars. The dock lives permanently behind the monitor, every peripheral plugs into it once, and your laptop connects to the entire empire through one cable. Two buying rules keep you out of trouble. First, match the dock’s power delivery rating to your laptop’s charging wattage, a 65W dock will slow-charge a laptop that shipped with a 100W brick, especially under load. Second, check that the dock’s video output matches your monitor’s best input at full resolution and refresh rate; a QHD 100Hz panel deserves a dock that can actually drive it. Get those two specs right and the factory charger retires permanently to your backpack as a lecture-hall spare, which is exactly where it belongs. Zone 4: The Sanity Layer Small things carry outsized weight in a shared 12-by-15 room. A warm-temperature desk lamp does two jobs: it spares your roommate the overhead fluorescents during late sessions, and it gives your brain a light-based boundary between desk time and bed time, which matters more than it sounds when both happen within eight feet of each other. Cable management sounds like a personality quirk until you live with the alternative; a cable tray screwed under the desk lip, or even a strip of adhesive clips, keeps the floor vacuumable and the charger findable. A headphone hook on the desk edge saves your headset from the textbook avalanche. And a cheap desk pad unifies the whole surface visually, protects the university furniture from your deposit’s perspective, and doubles as a giant mousepad. None of these items costs more than a pizza, and collectively they are the difference between a desk that looks like a workstation and a desk that looks like a lost-and-found bin. The Build Order, on a Student Budget If the full setup outruns this month’s budget, buy in this order. Monitor first: it improves every hour at the desk, academic or otherwise, and the posture benefit compounds daily. Monitor arm second, because it multiplies the value of the space you just invested in. Keyboard third, when the laptop’s own keys start feeling like a compromise. Dock fourth, when the cable shuffle officially becomes annoying. Lamp, tray, and hooks fill stocking-stuffer gaps. Spread across a semester, no single purchase stings, and by finals week the whole system is humming. Verdict: Three Feet, Fully Weaponized One QHD monitor floating on an arm, one compact wireless keyboard, one dock, one lamp: that is the entire formula, and the core of it lands under $300 plus whatever dock your laptop deserves. It fits any dorm, packs flat for summer storage, and follows you to every apartment after graduation. Start with the screen, add pieces as the budget allows, and browse compact mechanical keyboards on Newegg when you are ready to upgrade the typing feel. Your spine and your GPA will both notice. title: Unicorn opportunity: Building internal audit from the ground up

body_text: Meet Omar Obaisi, based in Chicago, who leads our Global Internal Audit function at Amer Sports, overseeing SOX 404 compliance and operational audits. As his team focuses on advancing the audit program this year, they are deepening their role as a strategic partner, helping leaders anticipate risks, and creating tangible value across our growing global organization. Omar shares what makes Amer Sports a unique place for finance professionals and why he is excited about the future of finance at our company. You have an extensive career in finance. What made you choose Amer Sports? I’ve been fortunate to have built internal audit groups across my career, but this was a unicorn opportunity. The timing was rare—a newly public company with iconic brands, genuine global scale, and an internal audit function that still needed to be built. That combination doesn’t come along often. I wanted to be part of something formative rather than inherit a mature structure, and Amer Sports offered exactly that: a chance to build something meaningful from the ground up. In practice, that meant standing up the SOX program at a newly NYSE-listed company, establishing co-source relationships with Big 4 firms, and building audit governance directly with the Audit Committee. From your perspective as a finance leader, what sets Amer Sports apart for finance professionals? What struck me early at Amer Sports is the scope of what you’re exposed to: a world-class portfolio, globally scaled, operationally complex, spanning markets and business models most professionals never see in a single role. For a finance professional, that exposure is extraordinary. You’ve been here for two years now. What excites you most about where Amer Sports Finance is heading? We’re still in the early chapters of being a public company, and the finance organization is growing into that moment. What excites me is how much opportunity lies ahead for process maturity, for data-driven decision-making, for finance to earn a genuine seat at the strategic table. Investments like the Amer Sports Academy signal that leadership is serious about developing talent and setting the tone for strong cross-functional collaboration across regions, functions, and brands. That’s rare, and it matters. Most finance functions take years to move from compliance-first to insight driven. We have the opportunity to compress that timeline, and the organizational appetite to do it. Do you have a favorite memory from your time with us? Early in my tenure, the finance leadership team held our first team-building session in Shanghai. It was a chance to get to know each other on a more personal level, align on strategic plans and priorities, and establish how we would best support one another. The camaraderie in that room, and the genuine team-player culture the group was already building, set the foundation for everything that followed. body_text: BOSTON , July 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Haemonetics Corporation (NYSE: HAE) a global medical technology company focused on delivering innovative medical solutions to drive better patient outcomes, announced today that Martin Madaus has been elected to the Company's Board of Directors, effective July 24, 2026. Dr. Madaus brings more than 30 years of leadership experience in the diagnostics and life sciences tools industries, having helped drive corporate strategy, commercial growth and operational transformation as both a chief executive officer and a board member. He currently serves as Senior Operating Executive at The Carlyle Group, where since 2019 he has advised on healthcare investments and portfolio company performance. Previously, Dr. Madaus served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Ortho Clinical Diagnostics, Inc. (now QuidelOrtho Corporation), a global provider of in vitro diagnostics, where he led the company's business turnaround following its carve-out from Johnson & Johnson. Earlier, as Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Millipore Corporation, he led the company's transformation into a leading life sciences company, culminating in its acquisition by Merck KGaA in 2010. Before Millipore, Dr. Madaus served as President and Chief Executive Officer of Roche Diagnostics North America. In addition to his executive leadership experience, Dr. Madaus is an active board leader and currently serves as Chair of the Board of Repligen Corporation and as a member of the board of directors of Azenta, Inc. He holds a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from the University of Munich in Germany and a Ph.D. in Veterinary Medicine from the Veterinary School of Hanover in Germany. "Martin has built and transformed some of the world's leading healthcare companies and brings deep operational, commercial and strategic leadership experience to our Board," said Ellen Zane, Chair of Haemonetics' Board of Directors. "His track record of leading complex global organizations, driving operational excellence and creating shareholder value will be invaluable as Haemonetics continues to execute its strategy, expand its leadership across attractive end markets and deliver long-term value for patients, customers and shareholders." ABOUT HAEMONETICS Haemonetics is a global medical technology company dedicated to improving the quality, effectiveness and efficiency of health care. Our Apheresis business features proprietary technologies designed to enhance safety, yield, donor satisfaction and operational efficiency for plasma and blood collectors around the world. Our MedSurg business offers Blood Management Technologies to help inform treatment decisions and optimize the management of blood products, and Interventional Technologies, including advanced vascular closure systems and sensor-guided technologies, designed to drive procedural effectiveness and elevate the patient experience.
